````javascript
// ============================================
// LinkedIn Job Copier — Content Script
// ============================================
// Extracts job details from LinkedIn job pages
// and copies them to the clipboard.
//
// IMPORTANT: LinkedIn uses randomized/hashed CSS
// class names. This script relies on:
//   - href patterns (a[href*="/jobs/view/"])
//   - aria-labels
//   - text content matching
//   - DOM structure/relationships
// NOT on CSS class names.
// ============================================

(function () {
  'use strict';

  // ---- Constants ----
  const PREFIX = '[LinkedIn Job Copier]';
  const BUTTON_ID = 'ljc-copy-btn';
  const RESET_DELAY_MS = 2000;
  const SHOW_MORE_WAIT_MS = 600;
  const NAV_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 1000;

  // UI text lines to strip from descriptions
  const UI_TEXT_PATTERNS = [
    /^easy apply$/i,
    /^apply$/i,
    /^save$/i,
    /^saved$/i,
    /^share$/i,
    /^report$/i,
    /^show less$/i,
    /^show fewer.*$/i,
    /^see less$/i,
    /^see fewer.*$/i,
    /^show more$/i,
    /^see more$/i,
    /^…more$/i,
    /^\.\.\.more$/i,
    /^more$/i,
    /^try premium.*$/i,
    /^premium$/i,
    /^reposted$/i,
    /^promoted$/i,
    /^people also viewed$/i,
    /^similar jobs$/i,
    /^am i a good fit.*$/i,
    /^set alert.*$/i,
    /^follow$/i,
    /^message$/i,
    /^connect$/i,
    /^about the company$/i,
  ];

  // ---- 1. Logger ----

  function log(...args) {
    console.log(PREFIX, ...args);
  }

  function warn(...args) {
    console.warn(PREFIX, ...args);
  }

  function logError(...args) {
    console.error(PREFIX, ...args);
  }

  // ---- 2. Job Page Detection ----

  function isJobPage() {
    const url = window.location.href;
    return /linkedin\.com\/jobs\/(view|search|collections)/.test(url);
  }

  // ---- 3. Job Detail Panel Locator ----

  /**
   * Finds the currently-selected job detail panel.
   * LinkedIn uses randomized class names, so we locate the panel
   * by finding semantic anchors (job title link, "About the job" text,
   * Apply button) and then walking up to their common container.
   */
  function getJobDetailPanel() {
    // Strategy 1: Find the scrollable container in the right pane
    // that holds the job details. Look for a container that has both
    // a job title link AND an "About the job" section.
    const jobTitleLink = document.querySelector('a[href*="/jobs/view/"]');
    const aboutTheJobEl = findElementByText('About the job');

    if (jobTitleLink && aboutTheJobEl) {
      // Walk up from the title link to find a common ancestor
      // that also contains "About the job"
      let ancestor = jobTitleLink.parentElement;
      for (let i = 0; i < 15 && ancestor; i++) {
        if (ancestor.contains(aboutTheJobEl)) {
          log('Panel found via title+about-the-job common ancestor');
          return ancestor;
        }
        ancestor = ancestor.parentElement;
      }
    }

    // Strategy 2: Find the container holding the Apply button
    const applyButton = document.querySelector(
      'a[aria-label*="Apply"], button[aria-label*="Apply"]'
    );
    if (applyButton && jobTitleLink) {
      let ancestor = applyButton.parentElement;
      for (let i = 0; i < 15 && ancestor; i++) {
        if (ancestor.contains(jobTitleLink)) {
          log('Panel found via apply-button+title common ancestor');
          return ancestor;
        }
        ancestor = ancestor.parentElement;
      }
    }

    // Strategy 3: Find a scrollable div that contains the job title link
    if (jobTitleLink) {
      let parent = jobTitleLink.parentElement;
      for (let i = 0; i < 20 && parent; i++) {
        // Look for a scrollable container or a large container
        const style = window.getComputedStyle(parent);
        const isScrollable =
          style.overflowY === 'auto' ||
          style.overflowY === 'scroll' ||
          parent.getAttribute('scrollable') === 'true';
        const isLarge = parent.scrollHeight > 500;

        if (isScrollable && isLarge) {
          log('Panel found via scrollable ancestor of title link');
          return parent;
        }
        parent = parent.parentElement;
      }
    }

    // Strategy 4: Legacy class-based selectors (fallback for older LinkedIn layouts)
    const legacySelectors = [
      '.job-view-layout',
      '.jobs-search__job-details',
      '.scaffold-layout__detail',
      '#job-details',
      '[class*="jobs-details"]',
      '[class*="job-view"]',
    ];
    for (const sel of legacySelectors) {
      try {
        const el = document.querySelector(sel);
        if (el) {
          log('Panel found via legacy selector:', sel);
          return el;
        }
      } catch (e) { /* skip */ }
    }

    // Strategy 5: Use the job title link's largest reasonable ancestor
    if (jobTitleLink) {
      let best = null;
      let parent = jobTitleLink.parentElement;
      for (let i = 0; i < 20 && parent && parent !== document.body; i++) {
        if (parent.textContent.length > 300) {
          best = parent;
        }
        // Stop if we've reached a very large container (probably the whole page)
        if (parent.textContent.length > 50000) break;
        parent = parent.parentElement;
      }
      if (best) {
        log('Panel found via title link ancestor heuristic');
        return best;
      }
    }

    warn('Could not locate job detail panel');
    return null;
  }

  // ---- 4. Title Extraction ----

  function extractTitle(panel) {
    if (!panel) return null;

    const strategies = [
      // Strategy 1: Link that points to a job view URL (most reliable)
      () => {
        const links = panel.querySelectorAll('a[href*="/jobs/view/"]');
        for (const link of links) {
          const text = link.textContent.trim();
          // Job titles are usually substantial text in an anchor
          if (text.length > 3 && text.length < 200 && !isUIText(text)) {
            return text;
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 2: h1 inside the panel
      () => {
        const h1 = panel.querySelector('h1');
        if (h1) {
          const text = h1.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 2 && !isUIText(text)) return text;
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 3: h2 heading inside the panel
      () => {
        const headings = panel.querySelectorAll('h2, h3');
        for (const h of headings) {
          const text = h.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 3 && text.length < 200 && !isUIText(text)) {
            return text;
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 4: The job title link matching current URL's job ID
      () => {
        const jobId = extractJobIdFromURL();
        if (!jobId) return null;
        const link = document.querySelector(`a[href*="/jobs/view/${jobId}"]`);
        if (link) {
          const text = link.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 3) return text;
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 5: Global h1 (direct job URL pages)
      () => {
        const h1 = document.querySelector('h1');
        if (h1) {
          const text = h1.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 2 && !isUIText(text)) return text;
        }
        return null;
      },
    ];

    for (let i = 0; i < strategies.length; i++) {
      try {
        const result = strategies[i]();
        if (result) {
          log(`Title extracted via strategy ${i + 1}: "${result}"`);
          return result;
        }
      } catch (e) { /* strategy failed, try next */ }
    }

    warn('All title extraction strategies failed');
    return null;
  }

  // ---- 5. Company Extraction ----

  function extractCompany(panel) {
    if (!panel) return null;

    const strategies = [
      // Strategy 1: Link to company page (most reliable on modern LinkedIn)
      () => {
        const links = panel.querySelectorAll('a[href*="/company/"]');
        for (const link of links) {
          const text = link.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 1 && text.length < 100 && !isUIText(text)) {
            return text;
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 2: Element with aria-label mentioning company
      () => {
        const els = panel.querySelectorAll('[aria-label*="company"]');
        for (const el of els) {
          const text = el.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 1 && text.length < 100 && !isUIText(text)) {
            return text;
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 3: Text near the job title that looks like a company name
      // On LinkedIn, the company name typically appears right after the title
      // and before the location. Find the title, then look at the next
      // text elements.
      () => {
        const titleLink = panel.querySelector('a[href*="/jobs/view/"]');
        if (!titleLink) return null;

        // Walk up to the title's container, then look for the next sibling
        // or child elements
        let container = titleLink.parentElement;
        for (let i = 0; i < 5 && container; i++) {
          const companyLink = container.querySelector('a[href*="/company/"]');
          if (companyLink) {
            const text = companyLink.textContent.trim();
            if (text.length > 1) return text;
          }
          container = container.parentElement;
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 4: Global fallback
      () => {
        const link = document.querySelector('a[href*="/company/"]');
        if (link) {
          const text = link.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 1 && !isUIText(text)) return text;
        }
        return null;
      },
    ];

    for (let i = 0; i < strategies.length; i++) {
      try {
        const result = strategies[i]();
        if (result) {
          log(`Company extracted via strategy ${i + 1}: "${result}"`);
          return result;
        }
      } catch (e) { /* strategy failed */ }
    }

    warn('All company extraction strategies failed');
    return null;
  }

  // ---- 6. Location Extraction ----

  function extractLocation(panel) {
    if (!panel) return null;

    const strategies = [
      // Strategy 1: Look for location text near the company link.
      // On LinkedIn's current layout, the pattern is:
      //   Title (link) → Company (link) → Location (text) → Workplace type
      // The location is typically a text node near the company link
      // that contains a comma (City, State, Country).
      () => {
        const companyLink = panel.querySelector('a[href*="/company/"]');
        if (!companyLink) return null;

        // Walk up a few levels and scan all text-bearing elements
        let container = companyLink.parentElement;
        for (let i = 0; i < 5 && container; i++) {
          container = container.parentElement;
        }
        if (!container) return null;

        // Get all leaf text elements
        const walker = document.createTreeWalker(
          container,
          NodeFilter.SHOW_ELEMENT,
          {
            acceptNode: (node) => {
              // Only consider elements with direct text (not containers)
              if (node.children.length > 3) return NodeFilter.FILTER_SKIP;
              const text = node.textContent.trim();
              if (text.length > 3 && text.length < 100 && looksLikeLocation(text)) {
                return NodeFilter.FILTER_ACCEPT;
              }
              return NodeFilter.FILTER_SKIP;
            },
          }
        );

        let node;
        while ((node = walker.nextNode())) {
          const text = node.textContent.trim();
          if (looksLikeLocation(text) && !isUIText(text)) {
            return text;
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 2: Scan the top portion of the panel for location-like text
      () => {
        // The job header section is usually in the first ~30% of the panel
        const allElements = panel.querySelectorAll('span, div, li, p');
        for (const el of allElements) {
          // Skip description area
          if (isInDescriptionArea(el)) continue;

          const text = el.textContent.trim();
          if (
            text.length > 3 &&
            text.length < 100 &&
            looksLikeLocation(text) &&
            !isUIText(text) &&
            el.children.length < 3
          ) {
            // Verify this isn't a large container (should be a leaf-ish element)
            const parentText = el.parentElement?.textContent?.trim() || '';
            if (text.length > parentText.length * 0.3) {
              return text;
            }
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 3: Check for elements with location-related aria-labels
      () => {
        const els = panel.querySelectorAll(
          '[aria-label*="location"], [aria-label*="Location"]'
        );
        for (const el of els) {
          const text = el.textContent.trim();
          if (text.length > 2 && text.length < 100) return text;
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 4: Text between company and "About the job" section
      () => {
        const companyLink = panel.querySelector('a[href*="/company/"]');
        const aboutEl = findElementByText('About the job', panel);
        if (!companyLink || !aboutEl) return null;

        // Get the text content between company and About section
        // by scanning elements in document order
        const allEls = panel.querySelectorAll('*');
        let afterCompany = false;
        for (const el of allEls) {
          if (el.contains(companyLink) || companyLink.contains(el)) {
            afterCompany = true;
            continue;
          }
          if (el.contains(aboutEl) || aboutEl.contains(el)) {
            break;
          }
          if (afterCompany) {
            const text = el.textContent.trim();
            if (
              text.length > 3 &&
              text.length < 100 &&
              looksLikeLocation(text) &&
              el.children.length < 3
            ) {
              return text;
            }
          }
        }
        return null;
      },
    ];

    for (let i = 0; i < strategies.length; i++) {
      try {
        const result = strategies[i]();
        if (result) {
          log(`Location extracted via strategy ${i + 1}: "${result}"`);
          return result;
        }
      } catch (e) { /* strategy failed */ }
    }

    warn('All location extraction strategies failed');
    return null;
  }

  // ---- 7. Show More Expansion ----

  /**
   * Expands "Show more" / "See more" / "…more" sections
   * before extracting the description.
   */
  async function expandShowMore(panel) {
    if (!panel) return;

    let clicked = false;

    // Scope search strictly to the description area / "About the job"
    const aboutEl = findElementByText('About the job', panel);
    const scope = aboutEl
      ? (aboutEl.parentElement?.parentElement || aboutEl.parentElement || panel)
      : panel;

    // Strategy 1: Find clickable elements with "show more" / "see more" text strictly in description
    const clickables = scope.querySelectorAll(
      'button, a, [role="button"], span[tabindex]'
    );

    for (const el of clickables) {
      const text = (el.textContent || '').trim().toLowerCase();
      const ariaLabel = (el.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').toLowerCase();

      // Explicitly ignore Apply, Save, Share, Follow, or More Actions buttons
      if (
        ariaLabel.includes('apply') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('save') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('more actions') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('action') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('share') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('follow') ||
        text.includes('apply') ||
        text.includes('save')
      ) {
        continue;
      }

      const isShowMore =
        text === 'show more' ||
        text === 'see more' ||
        text === '…more' ||
        text === '... more' ||
        ariaLabel.includes('show more') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('see more') ||
        ariaLabel.includes('click to see more description');

      if (isShowMore) {
        // Avoid clicking "show more jobs/results"
        const parentText = (el.parentElement?.textContent || '').toLowerCase();
        if (
          parentText.includes('show more jobs') ||
          parentText.includes('show more results') ||
          parentText.includes('load more')
        ) {
          continue;
        }

        log('Clicking expand button:', el.textContent.trim());
        el.click();
        clicked = true;
      }
    }

    // Strategy 2: aria-expanded="false" buttons in description context only
    const collapsedBtns = scope.querySelectorAll(
      'button[aria-expanded="false"]'
    );
    for (const btn of collapsedBtns) {
      const ariaLabel = (btn.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').toLowerCase();
      if (ariaLabel.includes('apply') || ariaLabel.includes('save') || ariaLabel.includes('more action')) {
        continue;
      }
      log('Clicking collapsed aria-expanded button in description');
      btn.click();
      clicked = true;
    }

    if (clicked) {
      await sleep(SHOW_MORE_WAIT_MS);
      log('Waited for content expansion');
    }
  }

  // ---- 8. Description Extraction ----

  function extractDescription(panel) {
    if (!panel) return null;

    const strategies = [
      // Strategy 1: Find the "About the job" section and extract
      // everything after it. This is the most reliable approach on
      // modern LinkedIn since it doesn't depend on CSS classes.
      () => {
        const aboutEl = findElementByText('About the job', panel);
        if (!aboutEl) return null;

        // The description is in the element's next sibling(s) or
        // in the parent container after the "About the job" heading
        let descContainer = aboutEl.parentElement;

        // Walk up if needed to find a container that has substantial text
        for (let i = 0; i < 5 && descContainer; i++) {
          const textAfter = getTextAfterElement(descContainer, aboutEl);
          if (textAfter && textAfter.length > 50) {
            return cleanText(textAfter);
          }
          descContainer = descContainer.parentElement;
        }

        // Alternative: get all text content after "About the job" in DOM order
        const descText = extractTextAfterMarker(panel, aboutEl);
        if (descText && descText.length > 50) {
          return cleanText(descText);
        }

        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 2: Find the largest text block that comes after
      // the job title and company info
      () => {
        const titleLink = panel.querySelector('a[href*="/jobs/view/"]');
        if (!titleLink) return null;

        // Find all substantial text blocks in the panel
        const textBlocks = [];
        const divs = panel.querySelectorAll('div, section, article');
        for (const div of divs) {
          const text = div.textContent.trim();
          if (
            text.length > 200 &&
            text.length < panel.textContent.length * 0.9 &&
            !div.contains(titleLink)
          ) {
            textBlocks.push({ el: div, text, length: text.length });
          }
        }

        // Sort by length, get the largest that's not the whole panel
        textBlocks.sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length);

        for (const block of textBlocks) {
          // Validate it looks like a job description
          if (
            block.text.includes('\n') ||
            block.text.includes('•') ||
            block.text.includes('experience') ||
            block.text.includes('requirements') ||
            block.text.includes('responsibilities')
          ) {
            return cleanText(block.text);
          }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 3: Legacy class-based selectors
      () => {
        const selectors = [
          '.show-more-less-html__markup',
          '#job-details',
          '[class*="jobs-description-content"]',
          '[class*="description__text"]',
          '[class*="jobs-box__html-content"]',
        ];
        for (const sel of selectors) {
          try {
            const el =
              panel.querySelector(sel) || document.querySelector(sel);
            if (el && el.textContent.trim().length > 50) {
              return cleanDescription(el);
            }
          } catch (e) { /* skip */ }
        }
        return null;
      },

      // Strategy 4: DOM-based extraction — find the description container
      // by looking for the element that contains structured text
      // (paragraphs, lists, bold text)
      () => {
        const richTextContainers = panel.querySelectorAll('div, section');
        for (const container of richTextContainers) {
          // Look for containers that have rich content (lists, paragraphs)
          const hasList = container.querySelector('ul, ol');
          const hasParagraphs = container.querySelectorAll('p').length > 1;
          const hasStrong = container.querySelector('strong, b');

          if ((hasList || hasParagraphs) && hasStrong) {
            const text = container.textContent.trim();
            if (text.length > 200 && text.length < 15000) {
              return cleanDescription(container);
            }
          }
        }
        return null;
      },
    ];

    for (let i = 0; i < strategies.length; i++) {
      try {
        const result = strategies[i]();
        if (result && result.length > 50) {
          log(
            `Description extracted via strategy ${i + 1}, length: ${result.length}`
          );
          return result;
        }
      } catch (e) { /* strategy failed */ }
    }

    warn('All description extraction strategies failed');
    return null;
  }

  // ---- 9. URL Extraction ----

  function extractURL() {
    let url = window.location.href;

    // Clean tracking parameters
    try {
      const parsed = new URL(url);
      if (parsed.pathname.includes('/jobs/view/')) {
        url = parsed.origin + parsed.pathname;
      } else if (parsed.searchParams.has('currentJobId')) {
        // Search results page — construct the direct job URL
        const jobId = parsed.searchParams.get('currentJobId');
        url = `${parsed.origin}/jobs/view/${jobId}/`;
      }
    } catch (e) {
      // URL parsing failed, use as-is
    }

    // Fallback: canonical link
    if (!url || !url.includes('linkedin.com')) {
      const canonical = document.querySelector('link[rel="canonical"]');
      if (canonical) {
        url = canonical.getAttribute('href');
      }
    }

    log('URL extracted:', url);
    return url;
  }

  // ---- 10. Validation ----

  function validateJobDetails(details) {
    const errors = [];

    if (!details.title || details.title.trim().length < 3) {
      errors.push('Job title is empty or too short');
    }

    if (!details.company || details.company.trim().length < 2) {
      errors.push('Company name is empty or too short');
    }

    if (!details.description || details.description.trim().length < 50) {
      errors.push(
        `Description is too short (${
          details.description ? details.description.trim().length : 0
        } chars)`
      );
    }

    if (!details.url || !details.url.includes('linkedin.com')) {
      errors.push('URL does not look like a LinkedIn URL');
    }

    if (!details.location) {
      warn('Location not found — will proceed without it');
    }

    return {
      valid: errors.length === 0,
      errors,
    };
  }

  // ---- 11. Clipboard Formatting ----

  function formatForClipboard(details) {
    let output = '';

    output += `JOB TITLE:\n${details.title}\n\n`;
    output += `COMPANY:\n${details.company}\n\n`;

    if (details.location) {
      output += `LOCATION:\n${details.location}\n\n`;
    }

    output += `JOB URL:\n${details.url}\n\n`;
    output += `JOB DESCRIPTION:\n${details.description}`;

    return output.trim();
  }

  // ---- 12. Clipboard Copy ----

  async function copyToClipboard(text) {
    // Primary: modern Clipboard API
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      log('Copy successful via Clipboard API');
      return true;
    } catch (e) {
      warn('Clipboard API failed, trying fallback:', e.message);
    }

    // Fallback: execCommand
    try {
      const textarea = document.createElement('textarea');
      textarea.value = text;
      textarea.style.position = 'fixed';
      textarea.style.left = '-9999px';
      textarea.style.top = '-9999px';
      textarea.style.opacity = '0';
      document.body.appendChild(textarea);
      textarea.select();
      const success = document.execCommand('copy');
      document.body.removeChild(textarea);

      if (success) {
        log('Copy successful via execCommand fallback');
        return true;
      }
    } catch (e) {
      logError('execCommand fallback also failed:', e.message);
    }

    return false;
  }

  // ---- 13. Button Injection ----

  function injectButton() {
    if (!isJobPage()) {
      removeButton();
      return;
    }

    // Don't inject duplicates
    if (document.getElementById(BUTTON_ID)) {
      return;
    }

    const button = createButton();
    const injected = injectIntoActionBar(button);

    if (!injected) {
      log('Action bar not found, using floating button');
      button.classList.add('ljc-floating');
      document.body.appendChild(button);
    }

    log('Button injected');
  }

  function createButton() {
    const button = document.createElement('button');
    button.id = BUTTON_ID;
    button.type = 'button';
    button.setAttribute('data-state', 'ready');
    button.innerHTML = getCopyIcon() + ' <span>Copy Job Details</span>';
    button.addEventListener('click', handleCopyClick);
    return button;
  }

  function getCopyIcon() {
    return `<span class="ljc-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M16 1H4c-1.1 0-2 .9-2 2v14h2V3h12V1zm3 4H8c-1.1 0-2 .9-2 2v14c0 1.1.9 2 2 2h11c1.1 0 2-.9 2-2V7c0-1.1-.9-2-2-2zm0 16H8V7h11v14z"/></svg></span>`;
  }

  function injectIntoActionBar(button) {
    const applyBtn = document.querySelector(
      'a[aria-label*="Apply"], button[aria-label*="Apply"], [data-easy-apply-button]'
    );
    const saveBtn = document.querySelector(
      'button[aria-label*="Save"], button[aria-label*="Unsave"]'
    );

    // Strategy 1: Find the common parent row/container of Apply and Save buttons
    if (applyBtn && saveBtn) {
      let curr = applyBtn.parentElement;
      while (curr && curr !== document.body) {
        if (curr.contains(saveBtn)) {
          // Found the action buttons container row
          // Append as a dedicated sibling element at the end of the row
          curr.appendChild(button);
          log('Button appended to action bar row (after Save)');
          return true;
        }
        curr = curr.parentElement;
      }
    }

    // Strategy 2: If only Save or Apply is found, find the button's outermost wrapper
    const anchorBtn = saveBtn || applyBtn;
    if (anchorBtn) {
      let buttonWrapper = anchorBtn;
      // Walk up until we find a multi-child container or reach 3 levels
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        if (buttonWrapper.parentElement && buttonWrapper.parentElement.children.length > 1) {
          buttonWrapper.insertAdjacentElement('afterend', button);
          log('Button injected as sibling next to button wrapper');
          return true;
        }
        if (buttonWrapper.parentElement) {
          buttonWrapper = buttonWrapper.parentElement;
        }
      }

      if (anchorBtn.parentElement) {
        anchorBtn.parentElement.insertAdjacentElement('afterend', button);
        log('Button injected after anchor button parent');
        return true;
      }
    }

    // Strategy 3: Legacy class-based selectors
    const legacySelectors = [
      '.jobs-unified-top-card__actions',
      '[class*="top-card__actions"]',
      '.jobs-apply-button--top-card',
    ];
    for (const sel of legacySelectors) {
      try {
        const container = document.querySelector(sel);
        if (container) {
          container.appendChild(button);
          log('Button injected via legacy selector:', sel);
          return true;
        }
      } catch (e) { /* skip */ }
    }

    return false;
  }

  function removeButton() {
    const existing = document.getElementById(BUTTON_ID);
    if (existing) {
      existing.remove();
      log('Button removed');
    }
  }

  // ---- 14. Button State Management ----

  function setButtonState(state) {
    const button = document.getElementById(BUTTON_ID);
    if (!button) return;

    button.setAttribute('data-state', state);

    switch (state) {
      case 'ready':
        button.innerHTML = getCopyIcon() + ' <span>Copy Job Details</span>';
        break;
      case 'extracting':
        button.innerHTML = getCopyIcon() + ' <span>Extracting...</span>';
        break;
      case 'success':
        button.innerHTML = getCheckIcon() + ' <span>Copied!</span>';
        break;
      case 'error':
        button.innerHTML = getErrorIcon() + ' <span>Extraction Failed</span>';
        break;
    }
  }

  function getCheckIcon() {
    return `<span class="ljc-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M9 16.17L4.83 12l-1.42 1.41L9 19 21 7l-1.41-1.41L9 16.17z"/></svg></span>`;
  }

  function getErrorIcon() {
    return `<span class="ljc-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 2C6.48 2 2 6.48 2 12s4.48 10 10 10 10-4.48 10-10S17.52 2 12 2zm1 15h-2v-2h2v2zm0-4h-2V7h2v6z"/></svg></span>`;
  }

  // ---- 15. Click Handler ----

  async function handleCopyClick(event) {
    event.preventDefault();
    event.stopPropagation();

    log('Copy button clicked');
    setButtonState('extracting');

    try {
      // Step 1: Find the job detail panel
      const panel = getJobDetailPanel();
      if (!panel) {
        throw new Error('Could not find job detail panel');
      }

      // Step 2: Expand all "Show more" sections
      await expandShowMore(panel);

      // Step 3: Extract all job details
      const details = {
        title: extractTitle(panel),
        company: extractCompany(panel),
        location: extractLocation(panel),
        description: extractDescription(panel),
        url: extractURL(),
      };

      log('Extracted details:', {
        title: details.title,
        company: details.company,
        location: details.location,
        descriptionLength: details.description
          ? details.description.length
          : 0,
        url: details.url,
      });

      // Step 4: Validate
      const validation = validateJobDetails(details);
      if (!validation.valid) {
        logError('Validation failed:', validation.errors);
        throw new Error(
          'Could not extract job details: ' + validation.errors.join(', ')
        );
      }

      // Step 5: Format for clipboard
      const formatted = formatForClipboard(details);

      // Step 6: Copy to clipboard
      const copied = await copyToClipboard(formatted);
      if (!copied) {
        throw new Error('Clipboard write failed');
      }

      // Success!
      log('Copy successful!');
      setButtonState('success');
    } catch (err) {
      logError('Extraction/copy failed:', err.message);
      setButtonState('error');
    }

    // Reset button after delay
    setTimeout(() => {
      setButtonState('ready');
    }, RESET_DELAY_MS);
  }

  // ---- 16. SPA Navigation Detection ----

  function setupNavigationDetection() {
    let lastURL = window.location.href;

    // Method 1: URL polling
    setInterval(() => {
      const currentURL = window.location.href;
      if (currentURL !== lastURL) {
        log('URL changed:', lastURL, '→', currentURL);
        lastURL = currentURL;
        onNavigationChange();
      }
    }, NAV_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS);

    // Method 2: History API interception
    const originalPushState = history.pushState;
    const originalReplaceState = history.replaceState;

    history.pushState = function (...args) {
      originalPushState.apply(this, args);
      log('pushState detected');
      setTimeout(onNavigationChange, 300);
    };

    history.replaceState = function (...args) {
      originalReplaceState.apply(this, args);
      log('replaceState detected');
      setTimeout(onNavigationChange, 300);
    };

    window.addEventListener('popstate', () => {
      log('popstate detected');
      setTimeout(onNavigationChange, 300);
    });

    // Method 3: MutationObserver — watch for job content changes
    const observer = new MutationObserver((mutations) => {
      for (const mutation of mutations) {
        if (mutation.type === 'childList' && mutation.addedNodes.length > 0) {
          for (const node of mutation.addedNodes) {
            if (node.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
              const el = /** @type {Element} */ (node);
              // Check if a job-relevant element was added
              const hasJobLink = el.querySelector?.('a[href*="/jobs/view/"]');
              const hasAboutJob =
                el.textContent?.includes('About the job');

              if (hasJobLink || hasAboutJob) {
                log('Job content change detected via MutationObserver');
                setTimeout(onNavigationChange, 300);
                return;
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    });

    observer.observe(document.body, {
      childList: true,
      subtree: true,
    });

    log('Navigation detection setup complete');
  }

  function onNavigationChange() {
    removeButton();
    setTimeout(() => {
      if (isJobPage()) {
        injectButton();
      }
    }, 500);
  }

  // ---- 17. Initialization ----

  function init() {
    log('Initializing...');

    if (isJobPage()) {
      log('Job page detected, injecting button');
      setTimeout(() => {
        injectButton();
      }, 1000);
    } else {
      log('Not a job page, will watch for navigation');
    }

    setupNavigationDetection();
    log('Initialization complete');
  }

  // ---- Helper Functions ----

  function sleep(ms) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
  }

  function extractJobIdFromURL() {
    // Try /jobs/view/ID pattern
    let match = window.location.href.match(/\/jobs\/view\/(\d+)/);
    if (match) return match[1];

    // Try currentJobId query param
    try {
      const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
      const jobId = params.get('currentJobId');
      if (jobId) return jobId;
    } catch (e) { /* skip */ }

    return null;
  }

  function isUIText(text) {
    const normalized = text.trim();
    return UI_TEXT_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(normalized));
  }

  function looksLikeLocation(text) {
    if (!text || text.length < 3 || text.length > 100) return false;

    const locationIndicators = [
      /,/, // Contains comma (City, State)
      /\b(india|usa|uk|canada|australia|germany|france|remote|hybrid|on-site|onsite)\b/i,
      /\b[A-Z]{2}\b/, // State abbreviations
      /\b(new york|san francisco|london|bangalore|bengaluru|mumbai|delhi|pune|hyderabad|chennai|kolkata|toronto|sydney|berlin|paris|tokyo|singapore|dubai|noida|gurgaon|gurugram)\b/i,
      /greater\s+.+\s+area/i,
      /\bremote\b/i,
    ];

    return locationIndicators.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text));
  }

  /**
   * Find an element by its visible text content.
   * Returns the most specific (deepest) element that contains the text.
   */
  function findElementByText(searchText, scope) {
    scope = scope || document;
    const walker = document.createTreeWalker(
      scope,
      NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT,
      {
        acceptNode: (node) => {
          if (node.textContent.trim() === searchText) {
            return NodeFilter.FILTER_ACCEPT;
          }
          return NodeFilter.FILTER_SKIP;
        },
      }
    );

    const textNode = walker.nextNode();
    return textNode ? textNode.parentElement : null;
  }

  /**
   * Checks if an element is inside the job description area.
   */
  function isInDescriptionArea(el) {
    let parent = el;
    for (let i = 0; i < 10 && parent; i++) {
      if (parent.textContent?.includes('About the job')) {
        // Check if this is the description container
        // (contains "About the job" and has substantial text)
        if (parent.textContent.length > 200) {
          return true;
        }
      }
      parent = parent.parentElement;
    }
    return false;
  }

  /**
   * Extract text content that appears after a marker element in DOM order.
   */
  function extractTextAfterMarker(container, markerEl) {
    if (!container || !markerEl) return null;

    let foundMarker = false;
    let descriptionParts = [];

    // Walk the DOM tree in order
    const walker = document.createTreeWalker(
      container,
      NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT,
      null
    );

    let node;
    while ((node = walker.nextNode())) {
      if (!foundMarker) {
        if (node.parentElement === markerEl || markerEl.contains(node)) {
          foundMarker = true;
        }
        continue;
      }

      const text = node.textContent.trim();
      if (text) {
        // Stop if we hit known end markers
        if (
          text === 'About the company' ||
          text === 'People also viewed' ||
          text === 'Similar jobs' ||
          text === 'Show less'
        ) {
          break;
        }
        if (!isUIText(text)) {
          descriptionParts.push(text);
        }
      }
    }

    return descriptionParts.join('\n');
  }

  /**
   * Get text content that appears after a specific child element
   * within a container.
   */
  function getTextAfterElement(container, afterEl) {
    if (!container || !afterEl) return null;

    const children = Array.from(container.childNodes);
    let foundAfter = false;
    let textParts = [];

    for (const child of children) {
      if (child === afterEl || child.contains?.(afterEl) || afterEl.contains?.(child)) {
        foundAfter = true;
        continue;
      }
      if (foundAfter) {
        const text = (child.textContent || '').trim();
        if (text) {
          textParts.push(text);
        }
      }
    }

    return textParts.join('\n');
  }

  /**
   * Cleans raw text: collapses whitespace, preserves paragraphs and bullets.
   */
  function cleanText(text) {
    if (!text) return null;

    // Split into lines
    let lines = text.split('\n');

    // Filter out UI text lines
    lines = lines.filter((line) => {
      const trimmed = line.trim();
      if (trimmed === '') return true;
      return !isUIText(trimmed);
    });

    // Rejoin
    text = lines.join('\n');

    // Collapse multiple blank lines
    text = text.replace(/\n{3,}/g, '\n\n');

    // Clean up excessive spaces
    text = text.replace(/[ \t]{2,}/g, ' ');

    return text.trim();
  }

  /**
   * Cleans a DOM element's text for use as a job description.
   * Preserves structure from the DOM (paragraphs, bullet points).
   */
  function cleanDescription(element) {
    if (!element) return null;

    const clone = element.cloneNode(true);

    // Remove UI elements from the clone
    const uiElements = clone.querySelectorAll(
      'button, nav, [role="navigation"], footer, ' +
      '[class*="share"], [class*="report"]'
    );
    uiElements.forEach((el) => el.remove());

    // Convert DOM to text preserving structure
    let text = domToText(clone);

    // Clean the text
    return cleanText(text);
  }

  /**
   * Converts a DOM tree to text, preserving paragraphs and list items.
   */
  function domToText(node) {
    if (node.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE) {
      return node.textContent;
    }

    if (node.nodeType !== Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {
      return '';
    }

    const el = /** @type {Element} */ (node);
    const tag = el.tagName.toLowerCase();

    // Skip hidden elements
    try {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      if (style.display === 'none' || style.visibility === 'hidden') {
        return '';
      }
    } catch (e) { /* skip visibility check if it fails */ }

    const blockTags = [
      'p', 'div', 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6',
      'section', 'article', 'header', 'footer',
      'blockquote', 'pre', 'table', 'tr',
    ];

    if (tag === 'li') {
      const childText = Array.from(el.childNodes)
        .map((child) => domToText(child))
        .join('');
      return '\n• ' + childText.trim();
    }

    if (tag === 'br') {
      return '\n';
    }

    const childText = Array.from(el.childNodes)
      .map((child) => domToText(child))
      .join('');

    if (blockTags.includes(tag)) {
      return '\n' + childText.trim() + '\n';
    }

    return childText;
  }

  // ---- Start ----
  init();
})();
````

## File: linkedin-job-copier/README.md
````markdown
# LinkedIn Job Copier — Chrome Extension

A Chrome Extension (Manifest V3) that adds a **"Copy Job Details"** button to LinkedIn job pages. One click copies the job title, company, location, URL, and full description to your clipboard.

## Features

- **One-click copy** — Extracts and copies all job details in a clean format
- **Smart extraction** — Multi-strategy fallback system resilient to LinkedIn DOM changes
- **SPA-aware** — Detects navigation between jobs without page reloads
- **Auto-expands** — Clicks "Show more" / "See more" before extracting
- **Clean output** — Strips LinkedIn UI text, preserves paragraphs and bullet points
- **Visual feedback** — Button shows extracting/success/error states
- **Minimal permissions** — Only `clipboardWrite` and `activeTab`

## Installation

### 1. Download the Extension

Clone or download this folder (`linkedin-job-copier/`) to your computer.

### 2. Open Chrome Extensions

1. Open Chrome
2. Navigate to `chrome://extensions`
3. Enable **Developer mode** (toggle in the top-right corner)

### 3. Load the Extension

1. Click **"Load unpacked"**
2. Select the `linkedin-job-copier` folder
3. The extension should appear in your extensions list

### 4. Verify Installation

- Look for "LinkedIn Job Copier" in your extensions list
- Navigate to any LinkedIn job page (e.g., `https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/...`)
- You should see a blue **"Copy Job Details"** button

## Usage

1. Navigate to any LinkedIn job page
2. Click the **"Copy Job Details"** button
3. The button will show:
   - **"Extracting..."** — while collecting job data
   - **"Copied!"** — when successfully copied to clipboard
   - **"Extraction Failed"** — if something went wrong
4. Paste the copied content anywhere (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V)

### Clipboard Output Format

```
JOB TITLE:
Backend Engineer (Node.js / AWS / AI Systems)

COMPANY:
Prismforce

LOCATION:
Bengaluru, Karnataka, India

JOB URL:
https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/...

JOB DESCRIPTION:
Position: Backend Engineer (SDE-1 / Emerging SDE-2)
Experience: ~3 Years
...
```

## How to Test

### Basic Tests

1. **Direct job URL**: Go to `https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/XXXXXXXXX`
   - Button should appear
   - Click → verify clipboard content

2. **Job search**: Go to LinkedIn Jobs search, click on different jobs
   - Button should persist across job switches
   - No duplicate buttons should appear

3. **Page refresh**: Reload a job page
   - Button should re-appear

4. **Collapsed descriptions**: Find a job with "Show more" on the description
   - The extension should auto-expand it before copying

### Console Debugging

Open Chrome DevTools (F12) → Console tab and filter for `[LinkedIn Job Copier]`:

```
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Initializing...
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Job page detected, injecting button
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Job detail panel found via: .scaffold-layout__detail
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Button injected near action bar via: ...
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Copy button clicked
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Clicking "Show more" button
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Title extracted via strategy 1: "Backend Engineer"
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Company extracted via strategy 1: "Prismforce"
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Location extracted via strategy 2: "Bengaluru, Karnataka, India"
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Description extracted via strategy 1, length: 2345
[LinkedIn Job Copier] Copy successful!
```

## Extraction Fallback System

The extension **never relies on a single CSS selector**. Each field uses a ranked list of extraction strategies:

### Title Extraction (6 strategies)
1. `h1` inside the job detail panel (most reliable — LinkedIn uses h1 for titles)
2. Known top-card heading selectors (`[class*="top-card"] h1`)
3. Link matching the current job ID (`a[href*="/jobs/view/ID"]`)
4. Class-based selectors (`[class*="job-title"]`, `.t-24`, etc.)
5. First prominent heading in the panel (h1/h2/h3)
6. Global `h1` fallback for direct job URL pages

### Company Extraction (5 strategies)
1. Links to company pages (`a[href*="/company/"]`)
2. Known company-name class selectors
3. Structural: element near title with a company link
4. Subtitle text splitting (company · location format)
5. Global fallback with top-card scoping

### Location Extraction (4 strategies)
1. Known location/bullet class selectors
2. Subtitle text parsing (split by `·` separators)
3. Proximity scan near company info
4. Heuristic scan using location pattern matching (city/state/country patterns)

### Description Extraction (5 strategies)
1. `.show-more-less-html__markup` (very common LinkedIn class)
2. `#job-details` element
3. Known description container classes
4. `article` element within panel
5. Largest text block heuristic (finds the biggest meaningful text block)

### Why This Approach?

LinkedIn changes its DOM frequently. Class names like `jobs-unified-top-card__job-title` may be renamed, obfuscated, or restructured at any time. By using multiple strategies ordered from most-specific to most-generic, the extension gracefully degrades:

- If the primary selector breaks → the second one catches it
- If all class-based selectors break → structural/semantic fallbacks still work
- The `h1` tag, `a[href*="/company/"]` links, and `#job-details` are among the most stable anchors

## Architecture

```
content.js (single file, IIFE)
├── Logger (log, warn, error)
├── Job Page Detection (isJobPage)
├── Panel Locator (getJobDetailPanel)
├── Extractors
│   ├── extractTitle (6 strategies)
│   ├── extractCompany (5 strategies)
│   ├── extractLocation (4 strategies)
│   ├── extractDescription (5 strategies)
│   └── extractURL
├── Show More Expansion (expandShowMore)
├── Validation (validateJobDetails)
├── Formatting (formatForClipboard)
├── Clipboard (copyToClipboard)
├── Button Management
│   ├── injectButton / removeButton
│   ├── createButton
│   ├── injectIntoActionBar
│   └── setButtonState
├── Click Handler (handleCopyClick)
├── SPA Navigation Detection
│   ├── URL polling (1s interval)
│   ├── History API interception
│   └── MutationObserver
└── Init
```

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Button doesn't appear | Check chrome://extensions — is the extension enabled? Refresh the LinkedIn page. Check console for errors. |
| "Extraction Failed" | Open DevTools console, look for `[LinkedIn Job Copier]` logs to see which field failed. LinkedIn may have changed its DOM. |
| Wrong data extracted | The panel locator may be picking up the wrong section. Check the console to see which selector was used. |
| Duplicate buttons | This shouldn't happen (there's a duplicate check), but if it does, refresh the page. |
| Button in wrong position | The extension tries the action bar first, then falls back to a floating button. This is intentional. |

No background service worker, no remote connections, no data collection.
````

## File: backend/app/ai/provider.py
````python
"""OpenAI provider.

Wraps the OpenAI client and exposes a single typed method for structured
response generation.  The rest of the application never imports ``openai``
directly — all OpenAI interactions go through this class.
# Credit system: only /analyze costs 1 credit. All other AI ops are credit-free.

Responsibilities (AI Layer — architecture.md)
---------------------------------------------
- Construct and configure the OpenAI client.
- Call the Responses API with structured output format.
- Raise ``AIProviderError`` on any OpenAI error so callers receive a
  consistent exception type regardless of which provider is used.

Non-responsibilities
--------------------
- Prompt construction (handled by ``app.ai.prompts``).
- Business logic (handled by ``app.services.analysis_service``).
- HTTP concerns (handled by routes).
"""

from typing import TypeVar

from loguru import logger
from openai import APIError, APITimeoutError, OpenAI
from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.core.exceptions import AppError

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)


class AIProviderError(AppError):
    """Raised when the AI provider returns an error or unexpected response.

    Inherits from ``AppError`` so the global exception handler returns a
    consistent 500 JSON body without leaking provider details.
    """

    default_detail = "The AI provider returned an error. Please try again."


class OpenAIProvider:
    """Thin wrapper around the OpenAI Responses API.

    Instantiated once per request via dependency injection so that the API
    key and model can be reconfigured between test runs.
    """

    def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str, timeout: float = 30.0) -> None:
        if not api_key or not api_key.strip():
            logger.error("OpenAI API Key is empty or not configured.")
            raise AIProviderError(
                "OpenAI credentials are not configured. Please set the "
                "OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable in your .env file."
            )
        try:
            self._client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Failed to initialize OpenAI client", error=str(exc))
            raise AIProviderError(
                "Failed to initialize the AI provider. Please verify your credentials."
            )
        self._model = model
        self._timeout = timeout

    def parse_response(
        self,
        instructions: str,
        input_text: str,
        response_format: type[T],
        max_output_tokens: int | None = None,
    ) -> T:
        """Call the Responses API and return a validated Pydantic model."""
        logger.debug(
            "Calling OpenAI Responses API",
            model=self._model,
            response_format=response_format.__name__,
            max_output_tokens=max_output_tokens,
        )

        kwargs = {
            "model": self._model,
            "instructions": instructions,
            "input": input_text,
            "text_format": response_format,
            "temperature": 0,
            "store": False,
            "timeout": self._timeout,
        }
        if max_output_tokens is not None:
            kwargs["max_output_tokens"] = max_output_tokens

        try:
            response = self._client.responses.parse(**kwargs)
        except APITimeoutError as exc:
            logger.error(f"OpenAI API request timed out: {exc}")
            raise AIProviderError(
                "The connection to the AI provider timed out. Please try again."
            ) from exc
        except APIError as exc:
            logger.error(f"OpenAI API error (status={exc.status_code}): {exc}")
            raise AIProviderError(f"OpenAI API error: {exc}") from exc

        parsed = response.output_parsed
        if parsed is None:
            logger.error("OpenAI returned null parsed output")
            raise AIProviderError("The AI provider returned an empty response.")

        logger.debug(
            "OpenAI Responses API call complete",
            model=self._model,
            input_tokens=response.usage.input_tokens if response.usage else None,
            output_tokens=response.usage.output_tokens if response.usage else None,
        )

        return parsed  # type: ignore[return-value]

    def generate_text(
        self,
        system_prompt: str,
        user_prompt: str,
        temperature: float = 0.4,
    ) -> str:
        """Call OpenAI API for free-form text generation."""
        logger.debug("Calling OpenAI API for text generation", model=self._model)
        try:
            response = self._client.chat.completions.create(
                model=self._model,
                messages=[
                    {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
                    {"role": "user", "content": user_prompt},
                ],
                temperature=temperature,
                timeout=self._timeout,
            )
            content = response.choices[0].message.content
            if not content:
                raise AIProviderError("The AI provider returned an empty text response.")
            return content.strip()
        except APITimeoutError as exc:
            logger.error(f"OpenAI API request timed out: {exc}")
            raise AIProviderError("The connection to the AI provider timed out. Please try again.") from exc
        except APIError as exc:
            logger.error(f"OpenAI API error: {exc}")
            raise AIProviderError(f"OpenAI API error: {exc}") from exc
````

## File: backend/app/ai/review_prompts.py
````python
"""Unified review prompt builder.

Constructs the system instructions and user message for the recruiter-centric
unified review. This model evaluates the resume as a single cohesive document
to make trade-offs, deduplicate advice, and select high-impact improvements.
"""

from app.schemas.comparison import ComparisonResult
from app.schemas.job_description import JobDescription
from app.schemas.section import SectionItem

# ── Recruiter-Centric unified review instructions ───────────────────────────

REVIEW_INSTRUCTIONS = """\
You are a senior hiring manager, executive recruiter, and expert resume consultant reviewing a candidate's resume against a job description across any industry or professional domain (Engineering, Logistics, Customs, Sales, Operations, Finance, Management, Customer Service, Healthcare, Marketing, etc.).

Your objective is to evaluate the resume as ONE document and make strategic trade-offs on where improvements will yield the highest interview callback rates.

Strict Principles:
1. **Target Job Title**: Extract/derive a concise, highly specific 2-4 word target job title for `target_job_title` from the job description (e.g., 'Customs Clearance Specialist', 'Logistics Operations Manager', 'AI Application Engineer', 'Full Stack Developer').
2. **Recruiter-style Priority**: Do not suggest adding keywords to every section. Recommend at most FIVE overall Improvements, prioritized from 1 (highest impact) to 5.
3. **Deduplication**: If suggesting an improvement in one section solves the gap, do not repeat or duplicate the recommendation in any other section.
4. **Truthfulness and Evidence Reuse**: Never suggest inventing experience, achievements, dates, or certifications.
   - If a target technology (e.g. Next.js App Router, Tailwind) is missing, search the entire resume context first.
   - If supporting evidence exists elsewhere (e.g., they have React Native or vanilla React experience), suggest moving or highlighting it in the target section as an *adjacent* skill.
5. **Selective Section Status**: Assign section review status carefully:
   - `improve`: Active improvements supported by resume evidence. MUST BE ASSIGNED to Professional Experience, Projects, Skills, and Summary sections whenever keyword alignment is recommended.
   - `keep`: High-quality match containing 100% of required keywords and zero gaps.
   - `reduce_emphasis`: Strictly reserved for non-essential sections like Hobbies or Interests. NEVER mark main Experience, Work History, Projects, Skills, or Summary sections as 'reduce_emphasis'.
6. **Exact Section Name Matching**: Each `section_name` in your output MUST exactly match one of the section headers provided under === CANDIDATE RESUME === in square brackets. Do not duplicate recommendations across multiple roles.
7. **Strict Evidence-Gated Recommendations**: NEVER recommend adding, highlighting, or introducing a skill, language, framework, or technology in any section recommendation if that skill does NOT exist anywhere in the candidate's resume under === CANDIDATE RESUME ===. Recommend ONLY keywords/skills supported by candidate resume evidence.
8. **Concise Rationale**: Keep all explanations, reasons, and impact strings concise (1-2 sentences max per item).
"""


def build_review_input(
    sections: list[SectionItem],
    comparison: ComparisonResult,
    job_description: JobDescription,
) -> str:
    """Format the full job context, deterministic comparisons, and full resume content."""
    parts = [
        _format_job_context(job_description),
        "",
        "=== DETECTOR GAP ANALYSIS ===",
        f"Overall Match Coverage: {comparison.overall_coverage_percentage}%",
        f"Missing Skills: {', '.join(comparison.missing_skills)}",
        f"Missing Technologies: {', '.join(comparison.missing_technologies)}",
        "",
        "=== CANDIDATE RESUME ===",
    ]

    for section in sections:
        if section.normalized_name == "header":
            continue
        parts.append(f"[{section.title}]")
        for para in section.paragraphs:
            text = para.text.strip()
            if text and text.lower() != section.title.strip().lower():
                parts.append(text)
        parts.append("")

    return "\n".join(parts)


def _format_job_context(jd: JobDescription) -> str:
    """Format the minimal JD context needed for the review."""
    lines = ["=== JOB DESCRIPTION ==="]
    if jd.title:
        lines.append(f"Title: {jd.title}")
    if jd.experience_required:
        lines.append(f"Experience required: {jd.experience_required}")
    if jd.required_skills:
        lines.append("Required skills: " + ", ".join(jd.required_skills))
    if jd.technologies:
        lines.append("Technologies: " + ", ".join(jd.technologies))
    if jd.responsibilities:
        lines.append("Key responsibilities: " + "; ".join(jd.responsibilities[:5]))
    return "\n".join(lines)
````

## File: backend/app/api/v1/extension.py
````python
import io
import os
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse, JSONResponse
from app.dependencies.auth import get_current_user, get_optional_current_user
from app.models import User

router = APIRouter(prefix="/extension", tags=["extension"])

def get_extension_dir() -> Path:
    """Find the extension directory from known bundle/project locations."""
    candidate_dirs = [
        # 1. Bundled inside backend/app/extension_src
        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "extension_src",
        # 2. Mounted into container at /app/linkedin-job-copier
        Path("/app/linkedin-job-copier"),
        # 3. Development root locations
        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] / "linkedin-job-copier",
        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "linkedin-job-copier",
        Path("/opt/role_craft/linkedin-job-copier"),
    ]
    for p in candidate_dirs:
        if p.exists() and (p / "manifest.json").exists():
            return p
    return candidate_dirs[0]


def is_user_pro_or_elite(user: User) -> bool:
    """Check if the user is on Pro or Elite plan or has an active subscription."""
    if not user:
        return False
    plan = (user.plan_type or "").lower()
    return plan in ["pro", "elite"] or user.subscription_status == "active"


def build_extension_zip() -> io.BytesIO:
    """Builds a ZIP archive in memory containing all necessary extension files."""
    ext_dir = get_extension_dir()
    if not ext_dir.exists() or not (ext_dir / "manifest.json").exists():
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_500_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR,
            detail=f"Extension source files not found on server (checked {ext_dir}).",
        )

    zip_buffer = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_buffer, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(ext_dir):
            for file in files:
                # Exclude hidden files or git files if any
                if file.startswith(".") or file.endswith(".tmp"):
                    continue
                file_path = Path(root) / file
                arcname = file_path.relative_to(ext_dir)
                # Nest inside folder rolecraft-linkedin-copier/ inside the zip for clean extraction
                zf.write(file_path, arcname=f"rolecraft-linkedin-copier/{arcname}")

    zip_buffer.seek(0)
    return zip_buffer


@router.get("/status")
def get_extension_status(user: User | None = Depends(get_optional_current_user)):
    """Returns access eligibility status for the current user."""
    if not user:
        return {
            "authenticated": False,
            "eligible": False,
            "plan_type": "guest",
            "version": "1.0.0",
        }

    eligible = is_user_pro_or_elite(user)
    return {
        "authenticated": True,
        "eligible": eligible,
        "plan_type": user.plan_type,
        "version": "1.0.0",
    }


@router.get("/download")
def download_extension(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    """Downloads the RoleCraft LinkedIn Chrome Extension bundle (.zip).
    
    Protected route: Only available to Pro and Elite members.
    """
    if not is_user_pro_or_elite(user):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="The LinkedIn Chrome Extension is exclusive to Pro and Elite members. Please upgrade your subscription to access it.",
        )

    zip_buffer = build_extension_zip()
    return StreamingResponse(
        zip_buffer,
        media_type="application/zip",
        headers={
            "Content-Disposition": 'attachment; filename="rolecraft-linkedin-copier.zip"',
            "Access-Control-Expose-Headers": "Content-Disposition",
        },
    )
````

## File: backend/app/api/v1/support.py
````python
import json
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Optional
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from loguru import logger

from app.core.database import get_db
from app.dependencies.auth import get_optional_current_user
from app.models import User, IssueReport
from app.schemas.support import IssueReportRequest, IssueReportResponse

router = APIRouter(prefix="/support", tags=["Support & Issues"])

@router.post("/report-issue", response_model=IssueReportResponse)
def report_issue(
    payload: IssueReportRequest,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    optional_user: Optional[User] = Depends(get_optional_current_user),
) -> IssueReportResponse:
    """Submit a bug report, formatting error, AI quality feedback, or general inquiry.
    
    Saves to the database for administrative triage in the Admin Dashboard.
    """
    user_id = optional_user.id if optional_user else None
    user_email = payload.user_email or (optional_user.email if optional_user else None)
    now = datetime.utcnow()

    # Convert context dict to string if provided
    context_str = json.dumps(payload.context_data) if payload.context_data else None

    # 1. Save to Database
    issue = IssueReport(
        user_id=user_id,
        user_email=user_email,
        issue_type=payload.issue_type,
        subject=payload.subject,
        description=payload.description.strip(),
        context_data=context_str,
        status="open",
        created_at=now,
    )
    db.add(issue)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(issue)

    logger.info(
        f"📩 [Support Issue Received] ID={issue.id} type={issue.issue_type} "
        f"user_email={user_email or 'anonymous'} user_id={user_id or 'none'}"
    )

    return IssueReportResponse(
        success=True,
        report_id=issue.id,
        message="Thank you! Your issue report has been received and our engineering team has been notified.",
        created_at=now,
    )
````

## File: backend/app/api/v1/tailor.py
````python
"""Tailor API router.

POST /api/v1/tailor
    Run AI tailoring on the user's master StructuredResume for a given job description.
    Saves result as a TailoredResumeModel in DB.
    Returns tailored resume JSON + diff map for preview UI.

DELETE /api/v1/tailor/{tailored_id}
    Delete a saved tailored resume.
"""

import json
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.ai.provider import OpenAIProvider
from app.api.v1.auth import get_current_user
from app.core.config import get_settings
from app.core.database import get_db
from app.core.exceptions import BadRequestError, NotFoundError
from app.models import User, StructuredResumeModel, TailoredResumeModel
from app.schemas.structured_resume import StructuredResume
from app.services.tailor_orchestration_service import TailorOrchestrationService

from app.dependencies.limits import verify_auth_only

router = APIRouter(prefix="/tailor", tags=["AI Resume Tailor"])
settings = get_settings()


def get_ai_provider() -> OpenAIProvider:
    return OpenAIProvider(
        api_key=settings.OPENAI_API_KEY,
        model=settings.OPENAI_MODEL,
        timeout=settings.OPENAI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    )


class TailorRequest(BaseModel):
    job_description: str
    job_title: str
    job_company: Optional[str] = None
    job_id: Optional[str] = None


class TailorResponse(BaseModel):
    tailored_resume_id: int
    tailored_resume: StructuredResume
    diff: dict
    changes_count: int


@router.post("", response_model=TailorResponse)
def tailor_resume(
    request: TailorRequest,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    ai_provider: OpenAIProvider = Depends(get_ai_provider),
):
    """AI-tailor the user's master resume for a specific job description.

    Reads the master StructuredResume, rewrites summary/experience/skills
    to better align with the JD, saves as a new TailoredResumeModel, and
    returns the tailored content + diff for the preview UI.

    Credit-free: AI tailoring does not consume credits. Only /analyze costs 1 credit.

    The master StructuredResume is NEVER modified.
    """
    if not request.job_description or not request.job_description.strip():
        raise BadRequestError("job_description is required.")
    if not request.job_title or not request.job_title.strip():
        raise BadRequestError("job_title is required.")

    # Load master resume
    record = db.query(StructuredResumeModel).filter(
        StructuredResumeModel.user_id == current_user.id
    ).first()
    if not record:
        raise NotFoundError(
            "No master resume found. Please upload and parse your resume first."
        )

    master_data = json.loads(record.resume_json)
    master_resume = StructuredResume.model_validate(master_data)

    # Run tailor orchestration
    tailor_service = TailorOrchestrationService(ai_provider=ai_provider)
    tailored_resume, diff = tailor_service.tailor_full_resume(
        master_resume=master_resume,
        job_description=request.job_description,
        job_title=request.job_title,
    )

    # Update master resume JSON record in DB with tailored content
    record.resume_json = tailored_resume.model_dump_json()
    record.version += 1

    # Persist the tailored resume history record
    tailored_model = TailoredResumeModel(
        user_id=current_user.id,
        job_id=request.job_id,
        job_title=request.job_title,
        job_company=request.job_company,
        tailored_resume_json=tailored_resume.model_dump_json(),
        diff_json=json.dumps(diff),
    )
    db.add(tailored_model)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(tailored_model)

    return TailorResponse(
        tailored_resume_id=tailored_model.id,
        tailored_resume=tailored_resume,
        diff=diff,
        changes_count=len(diff),
    )


@router.delete("/{tailored_id}")
def delete_tailored_resume(
    tailored_id: int,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
    current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
):
    """Delete a saved tailored resume."""
    record = db.query(TailoredResumeModel).filter(
        TailoredResumeModel.id == tailored_id,
        TailoredResumeModel.user_id == current_user.id,
    ).first()
    if not record:
        raise NotFoundError(f"Tailored resume {tailored_id} not found.")
    db.delete(record)
    db.commit()
    return {"status": "ok", "message": f"Tailored resume {tailored_id} deleted."}
````

## File: backend/app/parsers/job_description_parser.py
````python
"""Job description parser.

Converts a plain-text job description into a structured ``JobDescription``
model using rule-based extraction only.  No AI, no external libraries
beyond the Python standard library.

This module is the Parser Layer for job descriptions.  It is intentionally
pure:

- Input:  str
- Output: JobDescription
- No HTTP, no services, no filesystem.
- All logic can be exercised with a plain string in a unit test.

Parsing Strategy
----------------
The parser works in two passes:

Pass 1 — Section splitting
    Scan lines top-to-bottom.  When a line matches a known section header
    pattern, subsequent lines (until the next header) are collected into
    that section's bucket.  Lines before the first header go into a
    special "preamble" bucket used for metadata extraction.

Pass 2 — Field extraction
    Metadata fields (title, company, location, etc.) are extracted from
    the preamble using small targeted patterns.
    List fields (responsibilities, skills, technologies, keywords) are
    produced by cleaning and deduplicating the collected lines.

Technology extraction uses a curated allow-list of known tech terms that
are matched against the full text, making it independent of the section
structure of a particular job posting.

Keyword extraction uses word-frequency analysis on the full text,
preferring nouns longer than four characters that appear more than once.
"""

import re
from collections import Counter

from app.schemas.job_description import JobDescription

# ── Section header patterns ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Each entry maps a regex (matched case-insensitively against a stripped
# line) to the internal bucket name it fills.  Order matters only for
# display; matching always uses the full list.

_SECTION_PATTERNS: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
    # Responsibilities
    (r"responsibilities", "responsibilities"),
    (r"what you.ll do", "responsibilities"),
    (r"^role$", "responsibilities"),
    (r"key responsibilities", "responsibilities"),
    (r"job duties", "responsibilities"),
    (r"duties", "responsibilities"),
    # Required skills
    (r"what we.re looking for", "required_skills"),
    (r"requirements?$", "required_skills"),
    (r"required skills?", "required_skills"),
    (r"qualifications?", "required_skills"),
    (r"must[- ]have", "required_skills"),
    (r"what you.ll need", "required_skills"),
    (r"you (will|must) have", "required_skills"),
    (r"minimum qualifications?", "required_skills"),
    # Preferred skills
    (r"preferred", "preferred_skills"),
    (r"nice[- ]to[- ]have", "preferred_skills"),
    (r"bonus", "preferred_skills"),
    (r"good[- ]to[- ]have", "preferred_skills"),
    (r"desired", "preferred_skills"),
    (r"plus(es)?$", "preferred_skills"),
    # Technologies (merged into technologies list)
    (r"tech(nologies|nical) stack", "technologies"),
    (r"tools? (and|&) technologies", "technologies"),
    # Benefits, perks, company info, and web page noise – collect but ignore
    (r"about (us|the (company|role|team|goodspace))", "_ignore"),
    (r"benefits?$", "_ignore"),
    (r"perks?$", "_ignore"),
    (r"what we offer", "_ignore"),

    (r"messagingyou are on", "_ignore"),
    (r"people you can reach out to", "_ignore"),

    (r"show match details", "_ignore"),
]
````
